question: Which wiki editor style should be the default?
context: Both editors are built so you can try them on real pages (Wiki tab, toggle in the toolbar). Pick the default; the other can stay as an option or be removed to cut code in gui/wiki.js.

options.name: Source + Preview (Obsidian-style)
options.what_it_is: You type markdown in a code-style editor on the left and see the rendered page update live on the right. What you type is exactly what gets saved.
options.how_it_fits_here: Already the CodeMirror 6 editor in gui/wiki.js. Files stay byte-for-byte what you typed, which keeps git diffs clean and AI edits predictable.
pros: AI-written blocks visibly tinted in the source
Same files open cleanly in Obsidian
cons: Split view needs a wide screen
options.reversibility_why: Default is one localStorage key; both modes already exist.

links.maturity: CodeMirror 6, mature, used by Obsidian and Replit

options.name: Rich (Notion-style)
options.what_it_is: You edit the rendered page directly: headings look like headings, checkboxes are clickable, no markdown syntax visible.
options.how_it_fits_here: Already built in gui/wiki.js with contenteditable + turndown converting back to markdown on save. AI blocks are read-only in this mode to stay lossless.
pros: One column, works on narrow screens
cons: HTML→markdown conversion can reformat unusual markdown
Diagrams must be edited in Source mode

options.name: Upgrade Rich to a block editor (TipTap/ProseMirror)
options.what_it_is: A real structured editor library (what Notion-like apps use) with drag handles, proper undo, and schema-validated content.
options.how_it_fits_here: Replaces the contenteditable code in gui/wiki.js with TipTap plus a markdown extension; adds ~300KB to the bundle and a new dependency tree.
cons: Markdown round-trip still not perfectly lossless
options.reversibility_why: Editor code would be rewritten around its API.

recommendation.why: The wiki is also the AI's memory. Lossless markdown keeps AI edits and git diffs exact, and the AI-block tint is clearest in source.
recommendation.would_change_mind_if: mostly non-developers will write in the wiki
